precepts.text: The Levites are taken from among the children of Israel as a gift to do the service of the tabernacle; that is why every tribe gave them cities.
precepts.point: The commandment was fulfilled when Israel came into the land: the heads of the fathers of the Levites came to Eleazar the priest and Joshua at Shiloh and claimed the cities the Lord commanded by the hand of Moses.

note.label: Numbers 35: The Cities of the Levites and the Cities of Refuge

precepts.why:
The tribes were commanded to give the Levites cities to dwell in out of their own inheritance, with suburbs round about them. Why did the Levites need cities inside every tribe’s territory? “And I, behold, I have taken your brethren the Levites from among the children of Israel: to you they are given as a gift for the Lord, to do the service of the tabernacle of the congregation.”

The Levites were taken from among the children of Israel as a gift, to do the service of the tabernacle. Every tribe needed that service done among them, so the Levites had to be spread out through all the children of Israel. That is why every tribe gave them cities.

precepts.text: When Israel reached the land, the Levites claimed the commandment of Numbers 35 and the children of Israel gave them cities and suburbs out of their inheritance.
precepts.point: The commandment was fulfilled when Israel came into the land: the heads of the fathers of the Levites came to Eleazar the priest and Joshua at Shiloh and claimed the cities the Lord commanded by the hand of Moses.

note.label: Numbers 35: The Cities of the Levites and the Cities of Refuge

precepts.why:
The commandment of Numbers 35 was fulfilled when Israel came into the land. “Then came near the heads of the fathers of the Levites unto Eleazar the priest, and unto Joshua the son of Nun, and unto the heads of the fathers of the tribes of the children of Israel; And they spake unto them at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, saying, The Lord commanded by the hand of Moses to give us cities to dwell in, with the suburbs thereof for our cattle.”

The Levites claimed what the Lord commanded by the hand of Moses. “And the children of Israel gave unto the Levites out of their inheritance, at the commandment of the Lord, these cities and their suburbs.” What Moses commanded in the plains of Moab, Joshua carried out at Shiloh.

precepts.text: He that smiteth a man that he die is put to death; but for him that lay not in wait, God delivering him into his hand, a place was appointed to flee; the presumptuous slayer is taken even from the altar to die.
precepts.point: The law itself was already instituted in Exodus 21; Numbers 35 answers where the manslayer goes: the Most High appointed him a place to flee.

note.label: Numbers 35: The Cities of the Levites and the Cities of Refuge

precepts.why:
Among the forty and eight cities of the Levites, six were “cities for refuge, which ye shall appoint for the manslayer, that he may flee thither.” Why would the Lord permit a manslayer refuge? The Most High gave Moses the understanding of how to discern manslaughter from murder, and the law itself was already instituted in Exodus 21.

“He that smiteth a man, so that he die, shall be surely put to death. And if a man lie not in wait, but God deliver him into his hand; then I will appoint thee a place whither he shall flee.” For murder there was no refuge; for manslaughter, where a man lay not in wait but God delivered the other into his hand, the Lord promised to appoint a place to flee.

“But if a man come presumptuously upon his neighbour, to slay him with guile; thou shalt take him from mine altar, that he may die.” The presumptuous slayer is taken even from the altar to die. Numbers 35 answers where the manslayer goes: the six cities are the place the Most High appointed him to flee.

precepts.text: The avenger pursues the slayer while his heart is hot; without refuge he would overtake and slay a man who was not worthy of death.
precepts.point: The city of refuge keeps the manslayer alive until he stands before the congregation in judgment, so the trial can discern between murder and manslaughter before the avenger reaches him.

note.label: Numbers 35: The Cities of the Levites and the Cities of Refuge

precepts.why:
The cities of refuge were for “the slayer” “which killeth any person at unawares”: he did not mean to do it; it was an accident that resulted in a death, and accidental deaths are of the Lord, beyond our control. Refuge means a condition of being safe or sheltered from pursuit, danger or trouble, and the manslayer is being pursued, for someone has the right to avenge the death of the one who was killed.

“Lest the avenger of the blood pursue the slayer, while his heart is hot, and overtake him, because the way is long, and slay him; whereas he was not worthy of death, inasmuch as he hated him not in time past.”

The avenger pursues while his heart is hot. Without a city of refuge close enough, he would overtake and slay a man who was not worthy of death, one who hated him not in time past. The city of refuge keeps the manslayer alive “until he stand before the congregation in judgment”, so the trial can discern between murder and manslaughter before the avenger reaches him.

precepts.text: At the mouth of two or three witnesses shall he that is worthy of death be put to death; one witness is never enough.
precepts.point: The rule stood first for sins worthy of death and then had to become the principle for every matter: two or three witnesses establish any accusation of iniquity or sin.

note.label: Numbers 35: The Cities of the Levites and the Cities of Refuge

precepts.why:
“Whoso killeth any person, the murderer shall be put to death by the mouth of witnesses: but one witness shall not testify against any person to cause him to die.” Witnesses, plural: “At the mouth of two witnesses, or three witnesses, shall he that is worthy of death be put to death; but at the mouth of one witness he shall not be put to death.”

Multiple people must testify, and their stories must match in the details for the murder to be established. One witness alone is never enough to put a man to death, because a single witness could lie in the interest of the avenger and put an innocent man to death.

precepts.text: One witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity or any sin; at the mouth of two or three witnesses is the matter established.
precepts.point: The rule stood first for sins worthy of death and then had to become the principle for every matter: two or three witnesses establish any accusation of iniquity or sin.

note.label: Numbers 35: The Cities of the Levites and the Cities of Refuge

precepts.why:
The rule of witnesses stood first for sins worthy of death, and then it had to become the principle for every matter. “One witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity, or for any sin, in any sin that he sinneth: at the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses, shall the matter be established.”

Not only murder: any iniquity, any sin, in any sin that he sinneth. Two or three witnesses establish any accusation, so that no man is condemned on the word of one who might be lying.

precepts.text: Judges in all thy gates must judge with just judgment, respect no persons, and take no gift, for a gift doth blind the eyes of the wise.
precepts.point: Israel's judges later fell into exactly this: they became covetous and took bribes to clear the guilty and turn aside the poor in the gate.

note.label: Numbers 35: The Cities of the Levites and the Cities of Refuge

precepts.why:
The judges could “take no satisfaction for the life of a murderer, which is guilty of death”, and no satisfaction for the manslayer to come home before the death of the priest. A guilty man cannot buy himself off.

“Judges and officers shalt thou make thee in all thy gates, which the Lord thy God giveth thee, throughout thy tribes: and they shall judge the people with just judgment. Thou shalt not wrest judgment; thou shalt not respect persons, neither take a gift: for a gift doth blind the eyes of the wise, and pervert the words of the righteous.”

No matter who stands before the judge or what money is offered, if they are guilty of death they are guilty of death. A gift blinds the eyes of the wise and perverts the words of the righteous, which is why the judge in the gate may take none.

precepts.text: The judges of Israel came to afflict the just and take a bribe, turning aside the poor in the gate from their right.
precepts.point: Israel's judges later fell into exactly this: they became covetous and took bribes to clear the guilty and turn aside the poor in the gate.

note.label: Numbers 35: The Cities of the Levites and the Cities of Refuge

precepts.why:
Israel’s judges later fell into exactly what Numbers 35 forbade. “For I know your manifold transgressions and your mighty sins: they afflict the just, they take a bribe, and they turn aside the poor in the gate from their right.”

They became covetous and took bribes to clear the guilty and turn aside the poor in the gate. The satisfaction the law said never to take for a murderer became the bribe that afflicted the just, and the Lord counted it among Israel’s mighty sins.

precepts.text: Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed; the only cleansing of the land is the blood of the shedder.
precepts.point: That judgment was instituted back in the days of Noah, and Moses carried it forward in the statutes given to Israel, for the Lord himself dwells among the children of Israel.

note.label: Numbers 35: The Cities of the Levites and the Cities of Refuge

precepts.why:
“So ye shall not pollute the land wherein ye are: for blood it defileth the land: and the land cannot be cleansed of the blood that is shed therein, but by the blood of him that shed it.” The murderer who escapes his judgment leaves the land polluted.

That judgment was instituted back in the days of Noah: “Whoso sheddeth man’s blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of God made he man.” The only cleansing of the land is the blood of the shedder.

Moses carried it forward in the statutes given to Israel, and the reason is given: “Defile not therefore the land which ye shall inhabit, wherein I dwell: for I the Lord dwell among the children of Israel.”

precepts.text: The cities of refuge were appointed that the manslayer die not, until he stand before the congregation in judgment.
precepts.point: Notice the scripture says slayer, not murderer: a slayer may be innocent, it may have been a mistake or self-defense, so there are stipulations and laws for his case.

note.label: Joshua 20: The Cities of Refuge

precepts.why:
“Then ye shall appoint you cities to be cities of refuge for you; that the slayer may flee thither, which killeth any person at unawares. And they shall be unto you cities for refuge from the avenger; that the manslayer die not, until he stand before the congregation in judgment.”

This is the same law Joshua is applying: refuge from the avenger of blood for the one who killed at unawares. The city did not settle the matter; it kept the manslayer alive until he could stand before the congregation in judgment and his case be heard.

precepts.text: If he thrust him suddenly without enmity, or cast a stone seeing him not, the congregation shall judge between the slayer and the revenger of blood and deliver the innocent slayer back to his city of refuge.
precepts.point: The avenger of blood is a family member of the one killed, and while his heart is hot he is not thinking logically; he is guided by his emotions, and that is how you end up rendering evil for evil. Heart is hot is the same way we talk today, I was hot, I am heated: our forefathers and foremothers spoke the same way.

note.label: Joshua 20: The Cities of Refuge

precepts.why:
“But if he thrust him suddenly without enmity, or have cast upon him any thing without laying of wait, Or with any stone, wherewith a man may die, seeing him not, and cast it upon him, that he die, and was not his enemy, neither sought his harm: Then the congregation shall judge between the slayer and the revenger of blood according to these judgments”.

The innocent slayer, the one who killed without enmity and seeing him not, gets his case judged. “And the congregation shall deliver the slayer out of the hand of the revenger of blood, and the congregation shall restore him to the city of his refuge, whither he was fled: and he shall abide in it unto the death of the high priest, which was anointed with the holy oil.” So the refuge from the avenger of blood in Joshua 20 works like this: the congregation judges, the innocent slayer is delivered from the revenger and sent back to his city of refuge, and he stays there until the high priest dies.

precepts.text: The congregation shall restore him to the city of his refuge, and he shall abide in it unto the death of the high priest, which was anointed with the holy oil.
precepts.point: He also dwelt there until the death of the high priest of those days; then the slayer shall return to his own city and his own house, the city from whence he fled.

note.label: Joshua 20: The Cities of Refuge

precepts.why:
“And he shall dwell in that city, until he stand before the congregation for judgment”. The congregation had to see whether it was a mistake or intentional, questioning him on what he was doing and why, just like a courtroom. When the judgment came back that it was not intentional: “And the congregation shall deliver the slayer out of the hand of the revenger of blood, and the congregation shall restore him to the city of his refuge, whither he was fled: and he shall abide in it unto the death of the high priest, which was anointed with the holy oil.”

That is the “until the death of the high priest that shall be in those days” of Joshua 20:6. The slayer was restored to his city of refuge and abode there until the anointed high priest died; then he returned to his own city and his own house.

precepts.text: If the slayer comes outside the border of his city of refuge before the death of the high priest and the revenger of blood finds him and kills him, the revenger shall not be guilty of blood; the refuge is protective custody, and he was to remain in it.
precepts.point: He also dwelt there until the death of the high priest of those days; then the slayer shall return to his own city and his own house, the city from whence he fled.

note.label: Joshua 20: The Cities of Refuge

precepts.why:
The refuge was protective custody, and the slayer was to remain in it. “But if the slayer shall at any time come without the border of the city of his refuge, whither he was fled; And the revenger of blood find him without the borders of the city of his refuge, and the revenger of blood kill the slayer; he shall not be guilty of blood: Because he should have remained in the city of his refuge until the death of the high priest”.

If he stepped outside the border before the high priest died and the revenger of blood found him and killed him, the revenger was not guilty. “but after the death of the high priest the slayer shall return into the land of his possession.” That is the return in Joshua 20:6: “then shall the slayer return, and come unto his own city, and unto his own house, unto the city from whence he fled.”

precepts.text: The commandment by the hand of Moses: give unto the Levites cities to dwell in and suburbs round about them for their cattle, their goods, and all their beasts.
precepts.point: This was not a new request; it was commanded of the Most High by the hand of Moses that all twelve tribes should give of their inheritance to the Levites.

note.label: Joshua 21: The Cities of the Levites

precepts.why:
The heads of the fathers of the Levites came near to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua and to the heads of the tribes at Shiloh, saying, “The Lord commanded by the hand of Moses to give us cities to dwell in, with the suburbs thereof for our cattle.” This was not a new request. Here is the commandment: “Command the children of Israel, that they give unto the Levites of the inheritance of their possession cities to dwell in; and ye shall give also unto the Levites suburbs for the cities round about them. And the cities shall they have to dwell in; and the suburbs of them shall be for their cattle, and for their goods, and for all their beasts.”

It was commanded of the Most High by the hand of Moses that all twelve tribes should give of their inheritance to the Levites. Now that every tribe had its inheritance, the time had come to receive them, and the children of Israel gave the cities and their suburbs at the commandment of the Lord.

precepts.text: Cities of refuge were appointed that the slayer which killeth any person at unawares may flee there and not die by the avenger until he stand before the congregation in judgment.
precepts.point: The city of refuge worked like protective custody: the slayer that killed a person unawares fled there from the avenger of blood and stayed there until he stood before the congregation and his case was judged.

note.label: Joshua 21: The Cities of the Levites

precepts.why:
Hebron, given to the children of Aaron, was “to be a city of refuge for the slayer”. From the Q&A: not all the cities given to the Levites were cities of refuge. Only certain cities were designated for that. “When ye be come over Jordan into the land of Canaan; Then ye shall appoint you cities to be cities of refuge for you; that the slayer may flee thither, which killeth any person at unawares. And they shall be unto you cities for refuge from the avenger; that the manslayer die not, until he stand before the congregation in judgment.”

The city of refuge worked like protective custody: the slayer that killed a person unawares fled there from the avenger of blood and stayed there until he stood before the congregation and his case was judged. That is what Hebron was for the man that killed his brother accidentally.

precepts.text: Six cities were for refuge, three on this side Jordan where the two and a half tribes were and three in the land of Canaan, for the children of Israel, the stranger, and the sojourner.
precepts.point: The city of refuge worked like protective custody: the slayer that killed a person unawares fled there from the avenger of blood and stayed there until he stood before the congregation and his case was judged.

note.label: Joshua 21: The Cities of the Levites

precepts.why:
“And of these cities which ye shall give six cities shall ye have for refuge.” Six in all, out of all the cities of the Levites: “three cities on this side Jordan”, where the two and a half tribes were, “and three cities shall ye give in the land of Canaan”. Hebron in the hill country of Judah is one of the three in Canaan.

“These six cities shall be a refuge, both for the children of Israel, and for the stranger, and for the sojourner among them: that every one that killeth any person unawares may flee thither.” So the refuge was not only for Israel but for the stranger and the sojourner among them, for anyone that killed unawares.

precepts.text: If he smote him with an instrument of iron, a stone, or a hand weapon of wood so that he die, he is a murderer; the murderer shall surely be put to death, and the revenger of blood shall slay him.
precepts.point: The city of refuge worked like protective custody: the slayer that killed a person unawares fled there from the avenger of blood and stayed there until he stood before the congregation and his case was judged.

note.label: Joshua 21: The Cities of the Levites

precepts.why:
The refuge was for the man that killed his brother accidentally, not for the murderer. “And if he smite him with an instrument of iron, so that he die, he is a murderer: the murderer shall surely be put to death.” The same with throwing a stone wherewith he may die, or “an hand weapon of wood”: “he is a murderer: the murderer shall surely be put to death.”

“The revenger of blood himself shall slay the murderer: when he meeteth him, he shall slay him.” Hebron and the other five cities gave no protection from that.

precepts.text: If he thrust him of hatred or smote him in enmity, he that smote him shall surely be put to death, for he is a murderer.
precepts.point: The city of refuge worked like protective custody: the slayer that killed a person unawares fled there from the avenger of blood and stayed there until he stood before the congregation and his case was judged.

note.label: Joshua 21: The Cities of the Levites

precepts.why:
“But if he thrust him of hatred, or hurl at him by laying of wait, that he die; Or in enmity smite him with his hand, that he die: he that smote him shall surely be put to death; for he is a murderer”. Hatred, laying of wait, enmity: those mark the murderer, whatever he used, even his hand.

“the revenger of blood shall slay the murderer, when he meeteth him.” The city of refuge is for the slayer that killed at unawares; the man who killed of hatred could not hide in Hebron.

precepts.text: But if he thrust him suddenly without enmity, seeing him not, and was not his enemy, then the congregation shall judge between the slayer and the revenger of blood according to these judgments.
precepts.point: The city of refuge worked like protective custody: the slayer that killed a person unawares fled there from the avenger of blood and stayed there until he stood before the congregation and his case was judged.

note.label: Joshua 21: The Cities of the Levites

precepts.why:
“But if he thrust him suddenly without enmity, or have cast upon him any thing without laying of wait, Or with any stone, wherewith a man may die, seeing him not, and cast it upon him, that he die, and was not his enemy, neither sought his harm: Then the congregation shall judge between the slayer and the revenger of blood according to these judgments”.

This is the one Hebron was appointed for: sudden, without enmity, seeing him not, not his enemy. He fled to the city of refuge and stayed there in protective custody until he stood before the congregation and his case was judged between him and the revenger of blood, according to these judgments.

precepts.text: The revenger of blood himself shall slay the murderer; when he meeteth him, he shall slay him.
precepts.point: Joab had her act as a widow, saying the revenger of blood was coming for her last son. She knew, as Joab knew, that David was merciful, so she framed it around the law of the revenger of blood to draw out his mercy.

note.label: 2 Samuel 14: Joab Brings Absalom Home

precepts.why:
“The revenger of blood himself shall slay the murderer: when he meeteth him, he shall slay him.”

That is the law the woman of Tekoah built her story on. Joab had her act as a widow whose two sons “strove together in the field, and there was none to part them, but the one smote the other, and slew him.” Now the whole family said, “Deliver him that smote his brother, that we may kill him, for the life of his brother whom he slew”. By that law they would slay her last son and “quench my coal which is left”, leaving her husband “neither name nor remainder upon the earth.”

She knew, as Joab knew, that David was merciful, so she framed it around the revenger of blood to draw out his mercy. She asked the king “that thou wouldest not suffer the revengers of blood to destroy any more, lest they destroy my son”, and David swore, “As the Lord liveth, there shall not one hair of thy son fall to the earth.”

precepts.text: The suburbs of the Levites' cities reach from the wall outward a thousand cubits round about, for the cities have walls.
precepts.point: Asa has an army of 300,000 of Judah and 280,000 of Benjamin, all mighty men of valor.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 14: Asa Seeks the Most High and Finds Rest

precepts.why:
“And the suburbs of the cities, which ye shall give unto the Levites, shall reach from the wall of the city and outward a thousand cubits round about.”

The law measures from the wall of the city, for the cities of Israel have walls. So Asa built fenced cities: “Let us build these cities, and make about them walls, and towers, gates, and bars, while the land is yet before us.”

points: Moses commands the tribes to separate cities out of their own inheritance for the Levites to dwell in, with suburbs round about them.

The Levites needed cities inside every tribe's territory because the Most High took them from among the children of Israel as a gift, to do the service of the tabernacle of the congregation. Every tribe needed that service done among them, so the Levites had to be spread out through all the children of Israel.

The commandment was fulfilled when Israel came into the land: the heads of the fathers of the Levites came to Eleazar the priest and Joshua at Shiloh and claimed the cities the Lord commanded by the hand of Moses.

The law itself was already instituted in Exodus 21; Numbers 35 answers where the manslayer goes: the Most High appointed him a place to flee.

note.label: Numbers 35: The Cities of the Levites and the Cities of Refuge

This is the law given to Israel at that time, an understanding of those judgments; it is not license for anyone to go about killing today.

note.label: Numbers 35: The Cities of the Levites and the Cities of Refuge

points: Laying of wait means he was lurking and stalking, waiting to catch him slipping because of hatred between them; that is premeditated murder.

note.label: Numbers 35: The Cities of the Levites and the Cities of Refuge

points: Even without a weapon, smiting him in enmity with the hand so that he dies is murder; he that smote him shall surely be put to death.

note.label: Numbers 35: The Cities of the Levites and the Cities of Refuge

points: The law repeats its key words on purpose, the way legal statutes do, because the details decide the case: suddenly, without enmity, without laying of wait, and seeing him not.

note.label: Numbers 35: The Cities of the Levites and the Cities of Refuge

points: Seeing him not matters because it is nearly impossible to kill a man by accident while looking straight at him; the victim was out of sight when the thing flew and struck him.

points: If the slayer steps outside the borders of his city of refuge before that high priest dies and the revenger of blood finds him there and kills him, the revenger is not guilty of blood, because the slayer was instructed to remain within the borders.

note.label: Numbers 35: The Cities of the Levites and the Cities of Refuge

points: After the death of the high priest the slayer returns to the land of his possession, and the avenger can no longer touch him.

note.label: Numbers 35: The Cities of the Levites and the Cities of Refuge

points: The murderer is put to death by the mouth of witnesses, plural: multiple people must testify, and their stories must match in the details for the murder to be established.
One witness alone cannot cause a man to die, because a single witness could lie in the interest of the avenger and put an innocent man to death.
The rule stood first for sins worthy of death and then had to become the principle for every matter: two or three witnesses establish any accusation of iniquity or sin.

note.label: Numbers 35: The Cities of the Levites and the Cities of Refuge

points: The judges could take no satisfaction for the life of a murderer guilty of death, and no satisfaction for the manslayer to come home before the death of the high priest; a guilty man cannot buy himself off.
No matter who stands before the judge or what money is offered, if they are guilty of death they are guilty of death; a gift blinds the eyes of the wise and perverts the words of the righteous.

note.label: Numbers 35: The Cities of the Levites and the Cities of Refuge

points: Blood defileth the land, and the land cannot be cleansed of the blood shed in it but by the blood of him that shed it; the murderer who escapes his judgment leaves the land polluted.

note.label: Numbers 35: The Cities of the Levites and the Cities of Refuge

points: That judgment was instituted back in the days of Noah, and Moses carried it forward in the statutes given to Israel, for the Lord himself dwells among the children of Israel.
